# zlacp2

> Copies all or part of a real matrix `A` to a complex matrix `B`, setting imaginary parts to zero.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlacp2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlacp2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zlacp2( order, uplo, M, N, A, LDA, B, LDB ) → Complex128Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout<br>One of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'`. |
| `uplo` | `"upper" \| "lower" \| "all"` | Specifies whether to copy the upper triangle, lower triangle, or all of `A` |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | Input real matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A` |
| `B` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **out** · Output complex matrix |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `B` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`: Specifies the part of the matrix A to be copied to B.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular part
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular part Otherwise:  All of the matrix A
- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: The m by n matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, only the upper trapezium is accessed; if `UPLO = 'L'`, only the lower trapezium is accessed.
- `B`: On exit, $B = A$ in the locations specified by `UPLO`.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: `B`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "upper", "lower", "all"

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zlacp2.ndarray(
    uplo,
    M, N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB
) → Complex128Array
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `"upper" \| "lower" \| "all"` | Specifies whether to copy the upper triangle, lower triangle, or all of `A` |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | Input real matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` |
| `B` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **out** · Output complex matrix |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `B` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `B` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `B` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`: Specifies the part of the matrix A to be copied to B.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular part
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular part Otherwise:  All of the matrix A
- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: The m by n matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, only the upper trapezium is accessed; if `UPLO = 'L'`, only the lower trapezium is accessed.
- `B`: On exit, $B = A$ in the locations specified by `UPLO`.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: `B`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "upper", "lower", "all"
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zlacp2()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZLACP2`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zlacp2.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import zlacp2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlacp2';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const A = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface (copy the upper triangle):
let B = new Complex128Array( N * N );
zlacp2( 'row-major', 'upper', N, N, A, N, B, N );
console.log( reinterpret( B, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the ndarray interface (copy all of `A`):
B = new Complex128Array( N * N );
zlacp2.ndarray( 'all', N, N, A, N, 1, 0, B, N, 1, 0 );
console.log( reinterpret( B, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->
